projects.title: FRESHROUTE: cold chain for Serbian berries
projects.programme: Innovation Fund (synthetic)
projects.summary: FRESHROUTE addressed the systemic cold-chain weaknesses that reduce the competitiveness of Serbian raspberry, blueberry, and strawberry exports in EU markets. As academic partner, Professor Marković's team contributed validated predictive microbial growth models, MAP packaging specifications, and field sensor studies to a consortium that also included fruit exporting companies and a logistics technology provider. The project mapped temperature abuse events across 18 commercial export routes, quantified their microbiological consequences, and translated findings into revised pre-cooling protocols and MAP gas-mix recommendations adopted by partner exporters. A digital dashboard incorporating predictive shelf-life models was prototyped for real-time logistics decision support. FRESHROUTE resulted in three peer-reviewed publications, one conference presentation, and directly influenced cold-chain standard operating procedures at two partner export facilities, contributing to measurable reductions in consignment rejection rates at Western European destinations.

projects.title: Cross-Facility Vision Systems for Human Safety Monitoring in Smart Factories
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSVISION is a bilateral project addressing the deployment of overhead monocular vision systems across factory facilities in Serbia and Hungary, focusing on domain-generalisation challenges when the same detection software must operate in structurally different buildings. Gavrilović leads the work package on domain adaptation and scene-geometry estimation. The project involves three manufacturing partners who provide access to live production floors for data collection and system testing. Expected outputs include a transferable calibration toolkit, two joint journal publications, and a shared annotated dataset held under a cross-border data-sharing agreement. The project also supports student exchanges between the Faculty of Technical Sciences and the partner Hungarian faculty.

projects.title: Sensor-Driven Probabilistic Risk Models for SME Asset Management
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project developed a modular software pipeline for ingesting high-frequency IoT sensor streams, extracting interpretable statistical features, and fitting hierarchical Bayesian risk models suitable for small and medium enterprises that lack dedicated data science teams. Use cases were developed in collaboration with three SMEs in Vojvodina operating in food processing, cold-chain logistics, and metal fabrication. A reference implementation was released as open-source software. The project supported two PhD students and produced eight peer-reviewed outputs. A key output was a calibration protocol that allows a new site to obtain reliable risk scores after as little as 60 days of sensor history by borrowing strength from previously observed sites via the hierarchical model structure.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Autonomous Aerial Systems for Site-Specific Crop Protection in Cross-Border Agricultural Landscapes
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: AGROSKY developed and validated autonomous UAV spray systems for vineyards and row crops in the Vojvodina–Csongrád-Csanád border region. Jakovljević led the work package on real-time sensing and actuator integration, overseeing hardware development of the LiDAR–multispectral co-aligned payload and field trials across eight commercial farms. The project also addressed cross-border regulatory harmonisation for UAV operations and trained 24 local operators. Total budget allocated to the BioSense Institute component was approximately 320 000 EUR. Deliverables included two validated prototype UAV spray systems transferred to partner organisations and a joint technical standard for UAV spray system performance benchmarking adopted by all project partners.

projects.title: Sensor-Driven Precision Spraying: Closed-Loop Control Architectures for Low-Altitude UAV Applicators
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SENSPRAY addressed the gap between UAV canopy sensing and reliable real-time actuation by developing and formally verifying closed-loop control architectures for variable-rate spray systems. The project combined hardware-in-the-loop testing, outdoor flight experiments, and formal methods-based controller verification. Three PhD students and two MSc students were involved. Key outcomes included the coupled altitude–spray-rate controller described in the 2024 Computers and Electronics in Agriculture paper, a certified HIL test bench now available to external teams at BioSense Institute, and a draft technical report submitted to the Serbian Directorate of Plant Protection on performance requirements for commercially operated UAV spray systems. Budget: 49 800 000 RSD.

projects.title: Cross-Border Transport Protocol Interoperability for Multimedia Services in the Hungary–Serbia Corridor
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSTRANS investigated interoperability of QoS-sensitive multimedia transport protocols across national network operator boundaries in the Subotica–Szeged corridor. Mirjana Bošković led the work package on protocol conformance testing, which deployed passive measurement probes at four cross-border handover points to characterise DSCP re-marking behaviour and delay variation introduced by carrier-grade NAT. The project produced a conformance test suite, a jointly operated monitoring dashboard, and recommendations for bilateral peering agreements. Results informed network configuration changes at both the Serbian and Hungarian partner institutions, reducing inter-domain jitter for VoIP flows from 22 ms to 6 ms on the primary test path.
partners: University of Szeged, Department of Computer Science (Hungary)

projects.title: Preparative Purification and Stability of Microalgal Colourants for Use in Functional Foods
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: AlgColor examined the complete processing chain from biomass disruption through chromatographic purification to formulation and colour stability of C-phycocyanin and B-phycoerythrin targeting food and beverage applications. The project optimised tandem ion-exchange and hydroxyapatite purification at the 2 L preparative scale, characterised degradation kinetics under conditions relevant to beverage processing, and evaluated microencapsulation with maltodextrin and gum arabic as stabilisation strategies. Collaboration with the Department of Food Engineering at the Faculty of Technology provided access to spray-drying and shelf-life testing infrastructure. A laboratory-scale process manual and preliminary cost model were produced as industry-facing outputs. Total funding was 2.1 million RSD.

projects.title: Geodetic Methods for Reconstruction Planning of Ageing Underground Distribution Infrastructure
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: GEOMREKON investigates whether a combination of GPR surveys, precision GNSS and aerial photogrammetry can generate sufficiently accurate underground asset inventories to support cost estimation and route planning for distribution network reconstruction projects, replacing expensive manual test-hole programmes. The project tests three urban and two peri-urban study areas in the South Bačka and Srem districts. Deliverables include a decision-support GIS tool that flags cable and pipe segments exceeding age or condition thresholds based on as-surveyed depth, material classification and available failure records. The project involves doctoral supervision of two PhD candidates and collaboration with a regional electricity distribution operator providing access to maintenance records and operational data.

projects.title: Optimisation of Biochar Production from Vojvodina Agricultural Residues for Soil Amendment and Carbon Sequestration
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project systematically mapped the pyrolysis parameter space—temperature, residence time, and feedstock type—for the three dominant agricultural residues of Vojvodina: sunflower husks, wheat straw, and corn stover. Over 200 biochar samples were produced and fully characterised against European Biochar Certificate criteria. A decision-support matrix was developed to guide producers in selecting process conditions based on intended agronomic use (soil amendment versus carbon sequestration credit). Field verification was conducted through a two-season pot experiment in collaboration with the Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops. Results fed directly into four journal publications and one conference paper.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad

projects.title: Transition Metal Speciation and Removal in Cross-Border Watercourses: Tisa and Danube Sub-Basins
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border cooperation project addressed the speciation, transport, and removal of iron, manganese, copper, and chromium in shared watercourses. The Serbian team led by Prof. Žigić was responsible for the analytical work package, coordinating field sampling and laboratory speciation analysis at Serbian monitoring stations while partner laboratories in Hungary performed parallel measurements under identical protocols. Joint calibration exercises ensured inter-laboratory comparability; z-scores were within ±2 for all analytes. The project produced a harmonised sampling and analysis protocol for metal speciation in cross-border surface waters and a joint report submitted to the International Sava River Basin Commission. Serbian co-financing was provided by the Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research.
partners: Department of Environmental Engineering, Budapest University of Technology and Economics, Hungary
Directorate for Water Management of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Research Institute for Water Management, Budapest, Hungary

projects.title: Sealing Performance of Outdoor Electromechanical Enclosures under Pannonian Climate Conditions
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project set up a networked outdoor test rack with 24 instrumented enclosures across three sites in Vojvodina to collect simultaneous internal humidity, temperature, and condensation-event data over 30 months. Gasket specimens from each enclosure were retrieved at 10-month intervals for laboratory characterisation. The data collected formed the basis for the regression model relating enclosure configuration and gland fill ratio to condensation frequency, and provided field-correlation reference points for the accelerated ageing protocol developed subsequently. Two M.Sc. theses and one Ph.D. thesis were completed within the project scope.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Elektrovojvodina d.o.o., Novi Sad

projects.title: Modelling Moisture Transport and Condensation Risk in Sealed Enclosures for Low-Voltage Infrastructure
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: MOISTMOD targets the development of validated computational models for predicting moisture accumulation and condensation onset in sealed outdoor enclosures used in low-voltage electrical distribution infrastructure. The project combines laboratory climate-chamber experiments with two-dimensional coupled heat-moisture FEM simulations. A parametric study covering five enclosure sizes, three gasket materials, and four regional climate profiles is being conducted. An open-access Python-based tool for condensation-onset prediction is under development. The project involves collaboration with a meteorological data provider and an enclosure manufacturer. One postdoctoral researcher and two doctoral students are supported under the project.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Engineering, University of Kragujevac

projects.title: Sensor Node Energy Autonomy Through Accurate Cell Lifetime Modelling
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SENWATT aims to replace empirical rules of thumb for primary-cell sizing in long-lived IoT deployments with physics-informed parametric models calibrated on systematic laboratory ageing data. The project involves construction of an automated 48-channel pulse-load cycling station, a three-year ageing experiment on Li/SOCl₂ and Li/MnO₂ cells under nine IoT traffic profiles, and development of an open-source lifetime estimation library targeting resource-constrained microcontrollers. Validation deployments are planned in agricultural and hydrological monitoring networks in Vojvodina. A secondary objective is a public dataset of cell impedance and capacity data to support reproducible research in the field.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Chemistry, Technology and Metallurgy, Belgrade

projects.title: Danube Basin Environmental Sensor Infrastructure for Water-Quality and Flood Early Warning
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Romania–Serbia
projects.summary: DANUBESENS deployed a cross-border network of 120 water-quality and river-level sensor nodes along the Serbian and Romanian stretches of the Danube. Vuk Bačić contributed to the power-systems work package, responsible for specifying primary-cell types and sizes for each node class, defining adaptive duty-cycle policies to extend cell life in high-traffic alarm conditions, and conducting post-deployment energy audits using the embedded energy meters developed in his group. The project delivered 18 months of continuous monitoring data and a maintenance protocol for battery replacement scheduling.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Boundary-Scan Interconnect Integrity Monitoring for Automotive and Industrial PCB Assemblies
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: BOUNDLINK investigated whether periodic boundary-scan resistance measurements could serve as a non-destructive health indicator for BGA and fine-pitch connector solder joints in automotive-grade assemblies. The project combined accelerated life testing, four-wire resistance measurement through scan chains, and statistical process control methods to define alert thresholds for joint degradation. Results were validated against cross-section microscopy on a sample of 40 boards. The project delivered a monitoring protocol and a set of threshold tables for three thermal stress classes, and findings informed the design-for-testability guidelines developed in the subsequent THERMOTEST project.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Department of Electronics Technology, Budapest University of Technology and Economics

projects.title: Thermal and Mechanical Error Modelling for In-Process Accuracy Recovery in Articulated Robot Systems
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addressed the full chain from thermal field characterisation through unified error identification to embedded closed-loop compensation in six-axis industrial robots. Activities included instrumentation of three robot testbeds, design of a physics-based reduced-order thermal model, development of the unified geometric-thermal identification algorithm, and implementation of the extended Kalman filter recalibration scheme on embedded controller hardware. The project funded two doctoral researchers and one postdoctoral position. Experimental validation was conducted both in the university laboratory and at a partner company's assembly facility in Novi Sad. Deliverables included four journal publications, an open dataset of 90-day thermal drift records, and a software library for kinematic parameter management released under an open-source licence.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Accuracy-Driven Robot Integration in Small-Batch Manufacturing Across the Danube Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border cooperation project addressing the adoption of precision robot-based manufacturing by small and medium enterprises in Vojvodina and southern Hungary. Ivanović leads the work package on measurement methodology and error compensation, providing calibration services, training workshops, and transferable software tools to partner SMEs. Other work packages cover process planning, fixturing, and business model development. The project includes a shared demonstration cell installed at the University of Novi Sad and a mirror cell at the partner university in Hungary, enabling joint student supervision and staff mobility. Expected outputs include a calibration service protocol, training materials in Serbian and Hungarian, and at least two pilot implementations at industrial partner sites.

projects.title: Real-Time Scheduling and Replanning for Heterogeneous Robot Fleets in Partially Observable Environments
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addresses the problem of online task scheduling and motion replanning for fleets of 4–16 heterogeneous robots operating in warehouses and light manufacturing facilities where full observability cannot be assumed. The core research questions concern the computational complexity of replanning under partial observability, the design of anytime algorithms with bounded suboptimality guarantees, and the integration of task-level planning with geometric motion planning. Work packages cover algorithm design, benchmark development, hardware experiments on the Faculty's robot testbed, and technology transfer to a partner company developing logistics software. The project funds one PhD student and one postdoctoral researcher.
partners: University of Novi Sad, Faculty of Technical Sciences

projects.title: Cooperative Planning Methods for Cross-Border Autonomous Vehicle Deployments
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A bilateral Serbia–Hungary project investigating cooperative planning algorithms for small autonomous vehicle deployments at cross-border logistics terminals. The Novi Sad team leads the work package on combinatorial optimisation and scheduling, contributing multi-agent pathfinding algorithms adapted to the terminal environment. The Hungarian partner contributes simulation infrastructure and vehicle hardware. Ratko Simić leads the algorithmic work package, which is responsible for designing and validating the planning layer of the software stack. The project includes joint student mobility visits and a shared dataset of terminal operations collected at a pilot site near Subotica.
partners: University of Szeged, Department of Computer Science
TermiLog Hungary Kft., Szeged
University of Novi Sad, Faculty of Technical Sciences

projects.title: Reliability Data Infrastructure for Pneumatic Final Elements in Serbian Process Industry
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addressed the absence of locally calibrated failure rate data for pneumatic control and on-off valves in Serbian process plants. In collaboration with two Vojvodina refineries and a gas compression operator, a structured failure reporting and recording system was deployed at three facilities covering approximately 310 pneumatic final elements. Data were collected over 30 months and used to derive posterior failure rate distributions via Bayesian updating against generic OREDA entries. The project produced a pilot failure rate dataset covering five valve categories, a guidance document for plant operators on data collection procedures, and updated SIL verification calculation templates consistent with IEC 61511-1:2016. Results were disseminated to six partner companies through two industrial workshops held in Novi Sad.

projects.title: Functional Safety of Hybrid Control Architectures in Cross-Border Industrial Zones
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: HYSAFEX addressed the safety assessment of hybrid control systems at industrial facilities operating across the Serbian-Hungarian border region, where differing national implementation practices for IEC 61511 create inconsistencies in safety case documentation. Mladenović led the work package on methodology harmonisation, which produced a bilingual HAZOP facilitation guide and a set of common worksheets accepted by both Serbian and Hungarian regulatory reference bodies. The project included a joint training programme for 34 process safety engineers from 11 companies across the two countries. A shared database of cross-validated IPL credit claims was established and made available to participating facilities under a data-sharing agreement. The University of Novi Sad contributed its process control rig as a demonstration platform for cross-border functional testing exercises.

projects.title: Bio-Based and Biodegradable Synthetic Gear Lubricants for Enclosed Drive Systems: Formulation, Tribochemical Evaluation, and Environmental Fate
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: This project addressed the formulation and tribochemical characterisation of gear lubricants based on renewable base stocks, primarily phospholipid-modified vegetable oils and estolides, with zinc-free antiwear additive packages. The work combined laboratory tribological testing (four-ball, FZG, MTM), thermal-oxidative stability assessment (PDSC, RBOT), and surface analysis (XPS, AFM) to develop a performance comparison framework against conventional PAO-based references. Environmental fate was assessed through BOD/COD ratio measurements and OECD 301B biodegradability testing of the candidate formulations. The project involved collaboration with an agricultural research institute supplying modified crop-oil feedstocks and resulted in two journal papers, a conference contribution, and formulation guidelines submitted to a domestic gear-drive manufacturer.
partners: Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad, Serbia
Faculty of Mechanical Engineering, University of Belgrade, Serbia

projects.title: Nanoadditive-Enhanced Boundary Films in Industrial Gear Lubricants: Mechanistic Studies and Stability Assessment
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project investigates the tribochemical mechanisms by which graphene oxide and layered double hydroxide nanoadditives form protective boundary films on gear-steel contacts. Emphasis is placed on understanding the relationship between nanoparticle surface chemistry, dispersion stability in PAO and ester base stocks, and the resulting tribofilm structure as characterised by Raman spectroscopy, XPS, and AFM. A secondary objective is to establish the compatibility of these nanoadditives with commercial antioxidant and antiwear additive packages, including long-term storage stability under humidity cycling. The project involves one doctoral student and one master's student. Results are expected to inform formulation strategies for moderate-load enclosed gearboxes operating under intermittent lubrication conditions.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad, Serbia

projects.title: Dynamic Optimisation Methods for Real-Time Public Transport Management in Serbia
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project developed and validated rolling-horizon and online metaheuristic methods for real-time management of public bus fleets, focusing on disruption recovery and electric vehicle integration. The team built a simulation testbed using timetable and incident data from two Serbian cities, implemented a prototype decision-support tool for dispatchers, and produced a suite of open benchmark instances for dynamic vehicle scheduling. Collaboration with a regional transport operator provided access to anonymised operational data. The project supported two PhD students and resulted in five journal publications and three conference papers. A final dissemination workshop was held in Novi Sad in October 2024 with participants from transport operators, municipal authorities, and research groups from Hungary and Romania.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute for Transport Planning, University of Belgrade
Regional Public Transport Authority of South Bačka District

projects.title: Cross-Border Optimisation of Last-Mile Freight Logistics in the Danube Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSS-FREIGHT addresses the coordination of last-mile urban freight deliveries in border-zone cities in Hungary and Serbia, where different regulatory environments and infrastructure standards complicate joint scheduling. Obradović leads the work package on algorithmic methods, responsible for adapting multi-modal rolling-horizon scheduling tools to the specific constraints of cross-border freight zones, including customs clearance time windows and restricted delivery hours. The work package budget covers one postdoctoral researcher and computing resources. Progress is measured against a jointly developed benchmark suite. The project also includes stakeholder workshops with municipal logistics coordinators and small freight operators in Subotica and Szeged.

projects.title: Data-Driven Prognosis Framework for Rotating Machinery in Process Industries
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: PROGEN developed and validated a modular software framework for remaining useful life estimation of rotating machinery components—primarily bearings and gears—in pump, compressor, and gearbox applications. The project combined multivariate vibration and thermal feature extraction with a library of interchangeable prognosis model backends, including particle filters, Gaussian process regression, and LSTM networks. Experimental validation was conducted on purpose-built accelerated life test rigs at the Faculty of Technical Sciences and on instrumented equipment at two partner industrial sites in Vojvodina. The project produced open benchmark datasets for two failure modes, contributed to two journal publications, and trained three doctoral students. A lightweight deployable version of the framework was tested on embedded hardware at the end of the project period.
partners: Faculty of Mechanical Engineering, University of Niš, Serbia

projects.title: Harmonised Geodetic Reference Frames for Cross-Border Spatial Planning in the Danube Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: BORDERFRAME brought together geodetic institutions from Serbia and Hungary to address coordinate inconsistencies that hamper joint spatial plans and environmental monitoring along the Danube border. Mihajlo Kovačević led the work package responsible for datum comparison and residual analysis, overseeing joint GNSS campaigns at 40 common control points and the development of a unified transformation procedure for the border corridor. Outputs included a technical protocol adopted by both national geodetic authorities for cross-border survey projects, a shared dataset of border-zone control coordinates released under open licence, and a training workshop attended by 34 practitioners from both countries.

projects.title: Rule-Driven Parametric Artwork-to-Structure Registration for Sustainable Folding-Carton Production
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: PACKRULE addressed the gap between structural dieline design and graphic artwork placement in folding-carton production, where manual registration adjustments account for a disproportionate share of make-ready time and material waste. The project built a rule engine that reads a structural dieline in CFF2 format, extracts registered feature positions (score lines, cut edges, window apertures), and automatically constrains artwork element positions in a linked PDF document. Registration correction rules were derived from a database of 1,800 production runs covering four board grades and three printing processes. The project produced a validated software prototype, three journal papers, and two master's theses. One regional packaging converter participated as an industry observer and provided production data under a non-disclosure agreement.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Politehnica University Timișoara, Romania (associated partner)

projects.title: Cross-Border Knowledge Transfer in Color-Managed Packaging Prepress: Curriculum and Laboratory Development
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border project supported the development of shared teaching materials and laboratory protocols in color-managed prepress between the University of Novi Sad and the University of Pécs. Ildikó Papp led the work package responsible for harmonizing laboratory measurement procedures and developing a joint practical course module on ICC profile construction and verification. The project equipped both partner laboratories with matching measurement devices to enable reproducible inter-laboratory comparisons and produced a bilingual (Serbian–Hungarian) practical handbook distributed to over 140 students across both institutions during the project period. A joint summer school held in Novi Sad in 2020 attracted 38 participants from four countries.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Media Technology, University of Pécs, Hungary

projects.title: Framing Dynamics and Misinformation Checkpoints: Automated Detection Tools for Serbian-Language News
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: FRAMCHECK developed and validated a hybrid pipeline for detecting dominant news frames and potential misinformation markers in Serbian-language online news. The project combined an NLP preprocessing module adapted for Serbian morphology with a supervised frame classifier trained on a manually annotated corpus of 6,000 articles. A secondary strand produced an updated version of the Vojvodina Audience Panel questionnaire to include items on misinformation recognition and algorithmic awareness. Results were shared with two regional fact-checking organisations and with the journalism faculty at Novi Sad to inform curriculum updates.
partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Regional Media Literacy Centre Novi Sad (invented NGO)

projects.title: Formal Methods for Statutory Payroll Rule Representation and Automated Compliance Verification
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: This project investigated formal representations of Serbian statutory payroll rules with the goal of enabling automated compliance verification of ERP payroll modules against current legislation. The core output was a domain-specific language (DSL) for payroll rules with a formal semantics defined in terms of a small-step operational model. A model checker was implemented and used to verify four open-source payroll modules against a rule corpus covering the Labour Law, Personal Income Tax Law, and mandatory social contribution regulations as of 2023. The project produced four peer-reviewed publications, one M.Sc. thesis, and an open-source toolchain released under a permissive licence. Industry engagement included two workshops with ERP vendors and an advisory panel of payroll practitioners.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Applied Mathematics and Informatics, Niš

projects.title: Skills Transferability and Worker Reclassification During Manufacturing Technology Transitions
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: SKILLTRANS investigates how existing operator competency profiles map onto newly required competency profiles when manufacturing firms introduce automation or digitalisation investments, and what reclassification decisions result. The project combines longitudinal task-analysis observation at six Vojvodina plants undergoing technology transitions, analysis of internal HR reclassification records, and a structured employer survey covering 110 firms. The project develops and pilots a transferability index—a metric expressing the proportion of a worker's existing certified competencies that remain relevant after a defined technology change—and tests its predictive validity against actual reclassification outcomes. A practitioner toolkit for HR managers and a policy brief for the Serbian National Employment Service are planned as end-of-project deliverables.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Thermomechanical Modelling and Experimental Validation of Residual Stress Formation in Semi-Crystalline Injection Mouldings
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addresses a gap in predictive capability for residual stresses and warpage in injection-moulded semi-crystalline thermoplastics. The core activities include calibration of crystallisation kinetics models for PA6 and PP at industrially relevant cooling rates, implementation of a fully coupled thermomechanical simulation chain, and systematic experimental validation using in-mould sensors and post-ejection CMM and structured-light scanning. The project team of four researchers from the Faculty of Technical Sciences collaborates with the Faculty of Technology Novi Sad for DSC characterisation and with partners at the University of Maribor for material modelling. By the end of the project, a validated simulation workflow and a material parameter database will be made available as open data for Serbian polymer processing industry users.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad, Serbia
Faculty of Chemistry and Chemical Engineering, University of Maribor, Slovenia

projects.title: Optimisation of Mould Cooling Systems for Reduced Warpage in High-Volume Thermoplastic Production
projects.programme: industry contract
projects.summary: A two-year applied research contract with a regional plastic components manufacturer producing PP and PA6 parts for the automotive supply chain. The project objective was to reduce scrap rates caused by out-of-tolerance warpage in three production parts by developing and implementing a simulation-based cooling channel redesign procedure. The faculty team performed process simulation, surrogate-based optimisation of cooling channel geometry, and validation trials at the company's injection moulding facility. Scrap rates on the three target parts were reduced from an average of 6.8% to below 2.1% over a six-month production period following implementation of the redesigned moulds.

projects.title: Multivariate Monitoring Tools for Scale-Adaptive Film Coating in Solid Dosage Manufacturing

projects.title: Hydrolytic Stability of Halogenated Heterocyclic Intermediates Relevant to Agrochemical and Pharmaceutical Synthesis
projects.programme: industry contract
projects.summary: A contract research project with a regional chemical distributor and formulation company, assessing the aqueous stability of ten chlorinated and fluorinated heterocyclic building blocks under storage-relevant pH and temperature conditions. Experimental work was carried out entirely within the Faculty of Sciences laboratory. Deliverables included measured pH–rate profiles, recommended storage pH windows, and shelf-life projections at 5 °C, 25 °C, and 40 °C. Results informed the partner's product specification sheets. One co-authored technical report was produced; journal publication of selected data is planned.
partners: Hemikal d.o.o., Novi Sad
Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Valorisation of Vojvodina Agricultural Residues as Low-Cost Biosorbents for Textile Dye Removal from Industrial Wastewater
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project systematically screened eight Vojvodina-specific agricultural by-products as biosorbents for cationic textile dyes under conditions representative of Serbian textile industry effluents. Work included physicochemical characterisation (FTIR, XPS, BET, SEM-EDX), isotherm and kinetic modelling in batch mode, and column experiments using the two most promising materials. A laboratory-scale pelletisation protocol was developed in collaboration with the Faculty of Technical Sciences. Final deliverables included a ranked biosorbent database, a pre-screening procedure based on XPS surface composition, and publicly available sorption data. The project supported two MSc theses and one doctoral candidate.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Dynamic Modelling and Scale-Up of Pelletised Biosorbent Fixed-Bed Systems for Textile Effluent Treatment
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: DYNABED aims to bridge the gap between laboratory biosorption research and pilot-scale application by developing and validating dynamic mathematical models for pelletised biosorbent columns treating real mixed-dye textile effluents. The project combines experimental column campaigns at three scales (laboratory, bench, and a 50 L pilot unit to be constructed at the Faculty of Technical Sciences), mechanistic modelling of intraparticle mass transfer, and a machine learning layer for parameter estimation from easily measured biosorbent properties. Partners include a Slovenian university group with expertise in process modelling and a Romanian institute for pilot infrastructure. Two doctoral students are funded by the project.
partners: Faculty of Chemistry and Chemical Engineering, University of Maribor, Slovenia
National Institute for Environmental Research and Engineering, Cluj-Napoca, Romania
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Ecophysiology and Conservation of Biological Soil Crusts in Pannonian Steppe Habitats under Changing Precipitation Regimes
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: This project investigated how shifts in precipitation frequency and intensity, projected for the Pannonian region under climate change, affect the ecophysiological performance and community structure of biological soil crusts on loess and sand habitats in Vojvodina. Activities included long-term mesocosm experiments with manipulated rewetting regimes, seasonal field monitoring of antioxidant capacity and chlorophyll fluorescence, transcriptomic characterisation of dominant moss species under stress, and development of a UAV-based crust mapping protocol. A secondary objective was to provide baseline data supporting habitat management decisions at protected loess bank sites. Partners included the Institute for Nature Conservation of Vojvodina Province and the University of Szeged.
partners: Institute for Nature Conservation of Vojvodina Province, Novi Sad, Serbia
University of Szeged, Department of Ecology, Hungary

projects.title: Biodiversity Indicators for Loess Steppe Habitat Quality Assessment in the Serbia–Hungary Cross-Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border collaboration between Serbian and Hungarian partners aimed at harmonising biodiversity monitoring methods for loess steppe habitats listed under regional conservation frameworks. Hriešiková led the work package on cryptogamic indicators, contributing field survey data from 22 Vojvodina loess sites, developing standardised rapid ecophysiological assessment protocols, and co-authoring the joint indicator framework report. The project also included training workshops for conservation practitioners from both countries and a publicly accessible georeferenced database of loess habitat quality scores. Results were used by the Institute for Nature Conservation of Vojvodina Province in habitat management planning.
partners: Institute for Nature Conservation of Vojvodina Province, Novi Sad, Serbia
Kiskunság National Park Directorate, Kecskemét, Hungary
University of Szeged, Department of Ecology, Hungary
Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad, Serbia

projects.title: Karyotype Evolution and Genome Architecture in Polyploid Complexes of the Balkan Biodiversity Hotspot
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project addressed the mechanisms driving karyotype diversification in five polyploid plant genera endemic or near-endemic to the Balkans: Campanula sect. Medium, Dianthus sect. Plumaria, Onosma, Seseli, and Sesleria. Field sampling covered Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, and Montenegro. Laboratory work combined flow cytometry, FISH mapping of rDNA and satellite repeats, GISH for allopolyploid genome discrimination, and RepeatExplorer-based repeatome analysis from low-coverage genome sequencing. The project produced chromosome-level cytogenetic maps for 22 taxa, identified at least three independent polyploidisation events, and characterised four previously undescribed satellite DNA families. It funded two PhD students and supported two short-term research stays at partner institutions abroad.
partners: Institute of Botany, Czech Academy of Sciences, Brno
Faculty of Natural Sciences and Mathematics, University of Banja Luka
Faculty of Natural Sciences, University of Skopje

projects.title: Cytogenetic and Phylogeographic Diversity of Plant Endemics in the Dinaric Karst: Linking Genomic Data to Conservation Priorities
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: A cross-border cooperation project involving partners from Serbia and Hungary focused on rare and endemic plant species of the Dinaric karst and Pannonian margin. Turčan's group was responsible for the cytogenetic work package, delivering genome size estimates for 40 taxa, ploidy screening for 12 taxa with previously ambiguous chromosome numbers, and FISH-based karyotyping for eight priority species. Data were integrated with cpDNA phylogeographic results generated by the Hungarian partner. Project outputs included a shared database of cytogenetic and genetic data used to prioritise populations for ex situ conservation at partner botanical gardens. Three undergraduate thesis projects were carried out within the project framework.
partners: Institute of Biology, University of Pécs
Botanical Garden of the University of Debrecen
Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Resistance Mapping and Mechanism Characterisation in Dominant Arable Weeds of the Pannonian Plain
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aimed to produce the first systematic molecular resistance map for A. retroflexus and C. album across the major crop production zones of Vojvodina. Biotype collections were made in three annual sampling rounds from maize, sunflower, and soybean fields. Collected plants were characterised using whole-plant bioassays, target-site sequencing, CYP and GST activity profiling, and RT-qPCR. A georeferenced database of resistance mechanism frequencies was developed and shared with the Plant Protection Directorate of Serbia. The project also funded purchase of the laboratory's current real-time PCR platform and supported two PhD students co-supervised by Ranković. Results fed directly into several of the peer-reviewed publications listed in his profile.
partners: Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad
Faculty of Natural Sciences and Mathematics, University of Novi Sad
Plant Protection Directorate of the Republic of Serbia, Belgrade

projects.title: Coordinated Herbicide Resistance Surveillance in the Pannonian Agroecosystem: Serbia, Hungary, Romania
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: WEEDPAN is a trilateral surveillance project designed to detect new resistance cases and track the spread of resistance alleles across national borders in the Pannonian Plain. Ranković leads the work package on biochemical and molecular mechanism characterisation, while Hungarian and Romanian partners lead the field collection and geographic information system components respectively. Standardised sampling protocols were developed jointly to ensure cross-country comparability of bioassay results. The project includes a short-course training programme for national plant protection inspectors and plans a shared online database of confirmed resistance cases accessible to advisory services. First-year data covering 210 field samples from Serbia are currently being processed.
partners: Hungarian University of Agriculture and Life Sciences, Gödöllő, Hungary
University of Agricultural Sciences and Veterinary Medicine Cluj-Napoca, Romania
Institute of Field and Vegetable Crops, Novi Sad

projects.title: Genetic characterisation and conservation planning for Vojvodina Mangalica pig: from pedigree to genomics
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project aimed to establish the first comprehensive genomic database for the Vojvodina Mangalica population by combining SNP array genotyping of 600 registered animals with existing pedigree records spanning 25 years. Objectives included estimation of effective population size using both pedigree and linkage disequilibrium approaches, identification of runs of homozygosity, and development of a minimum-kinship mating algorithm suitable for use by the Vojvodina Mangalica Breeders Association. Đuro Mirković was responsible for the quantitative genetics component, including variance component estimation and breeding value computation. The project produced updated heritability estimates for production and reproduction traits and delivered a practical mating decision tool tested on two pilot farms.
partners: Institute for Animal Husbandry, Belgrade-Zemun
Vojvodina Mangalica Breeders Association, Novi Sad
Faculty of Veterinary Medicine, University of Belgrade

projects.title: Rumen Microbiome Responses to Bioethanol Co-products in Young Ruminants: Linking Fermentation Profiles to Growth Outcomes
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: RURUMIX examined how commercially available corn and wheat DDGS batches sourced from Serbian bioethanol plants affect rumen microbiome composition, fermentation end-products, and growth performance in dairy heifers from weaning to first service. The project combined in vitro fermentation assays, longitudinal in vivo trials at the university farm, and 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing to build a dataset linking batch sulphur and fibre variability to rumen outcomes. A decision support table for safe DDGS inclusion levels based on batch composition was developed and shared with extension services in Vojvodina. Three journal articles and two conference presentations were produced. The Faculty of Agriculture provided the animal housing, and the Institute of Molecular Genetics and Genetic Engineering in Belgrade contributed sequencing infrastructure.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Institute of Molecular Genetics and Genetic Engineering, University of Belgrade
Provincial Institute for Agriculture and Veterinary Medicine, Novi Sad

projects.title: Optimisation of pen design parameters for improved uniformity of growth in intensive beef bull production
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project investigated the combined effects of pen geometry, feeder configuration, and group size on within-pen variation in average daily gain in finishing Simmental bulls at the University of Novi Sad experimental cattle unit. Three pen layouts and two group sizes (8 and 16 animals) were tested in a factorial design over two production cycles. Primary outcomes were coefficient of variation in daily gain, displacement rate at the feeder, and feed conversion ratio. The project produced two peer-reviewed papers and a technical recommendation document distributed to provincial extension services. Total budget was approximately 2.4 million RSD.
partners: Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Provincial Secretariat for Agriculture, Forestry and Water Management, Vojvodina

projects.title: Enzymatic Synthesis of Functional Phospholipids for Liposomal Drug Carriers
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: ENLIPO addressed the complete production chain for pharmaceutical-grade phospholipids, from enzyme immobilisation and reaction optimisation through preparative purification to liposome manufacture and characterisation. The project established benchmarks for inter-batch variability, validated HPLC-ELSD and ESI-MS/MS analytical methods, and evaluated continuous packed-bed reactor operation as an alternative to batch synthesis. A collaboration with the Department of Pharmacy at the Faculty of Medicine, University of Novi Sad, provided access to in vitro cell-based permeability assays. The project supported one doctoral student and one postdoctoral researcher and produced six peer-reviewed publications. Infrastructure upgrades included a new cryo-TEM access agreement and a preparative HPLC system.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Department of Pharmacy, Faculty of Medicine, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Chemistry, University of Belgrade

projects.title: Pilot-Scale Continuous Production of Phospholipid Liposomes for Pharmaceutical Applications
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: LIPOSCALE focuses on transferring the continuous packed-bed reactor process developed under ENLIPO to a pilot scale of approximately 1 L/h throughput and integrating it with an inline membrane microextruder for liposome formation. The project evaluates process analytical technology (PAT) tools, including inline dynamic light scattering probes, for real-time liposome size monitoring. A key deliverable is a draft process description document suitable for technology transfer discussions with industrial partners. The project involves one master's student and provides analytical support from the University of Pécs under a bilateral agreement. Completion is expected mid-2025.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Department of Biochemical Engineering, University of Pécs

projects.title: Regulatory Harmonisation of Genotoxic Impurity Frameworks in South-East European Pharmaceutical Markets
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Romania–Serbia
projects.summary: REGIMPURE addresses divergences between Serbian and Romanian pharmaceutical impurity regulations as they relate to the transposition of EMA guidance on genotoxic impurities, including nitrosamines. Petrášová leads the work package on analytical method development and cross-laboratory validation. The project establishes a shared analytical platform between Novi Sad and Cluj-Napoca, conducts a joint ring trial with eight regional quality-control laboratories, and proposes aligned regulatory language for submission dossiers to both national agencies. A stakeholder working group including regulatory authority representatives and manufacturers from both countries meets quarterly to review draft guidance.
partners: Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Pharmacy, University of Medicine and Pharmacy Cluj-Napoca
National Agency for Medicines and Medical Devices of Romania
Medicines and Medical Devices Agency of Serbia
Alkaloid Farma d.o.o., Beograd

projects.title: Cross-Border Assessment of Pharmaceutical Pollutant Loads and Degradation Potential in the Danube Catchment
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: DANUPHARMA was a bilateral cross-border project jointly coordinated by the University of Miskolc (Hungary) and the Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad. The project mapped pharmaceutical pollutant concentrations at 24 shared monitoring points along the Hungarian–Serbian stretch of the Danube and its tributaries, using harmonised UHPLC-MS/MS analytical protocols developed and validated by both partner laboratories. Marija Uzelac contributed to method validation, field sampling during three seasonal campaigns, and LC-HRMS profiling of transformation products detected in river samples. The project produced a joint database of occurrence data, a harmonised risk quotient assessment, and a set of recommendations for cross-border water quality management submitted to relevant environmental authorities in both countries.
partners: Department of Environmental Engineering, University of Miskolc, Hungary
Tisza River Basin Authority, Nyíregyháza, Hungary

projects.title: Rational Solid-Form Selection for Poorly Soluble APIs: Integrated Screening and Scale-Up Workflows
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project established a tiered screening workflow integrating computational co-former selection (hydrogen-bond propensity and complementary functionality scoring) with experimental LAG, solution, and spray-drying screening for five poorly soluble APIs provided by a local formulation company. Characterisation relied on in-house PXRD, DSC-TGA, and Raman mapping, supplemented by access to solid-state NMR at a partner facility. Successful co-crystals were scaled to 50–100 g by twin-screw extrusion and assessed for dissolution improvement and physical stability under ICH storage conditions. The project trained two PhD students and produced eight peer-reviewed papers and three conference contributions.
partners: Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Pharmacy, University of Belgrade
Farmaceutski Zavod Vojvodina d.o.o., Novi Sad (industry partner)

projects.title: Cross-Border Knowledge Transfer in Pharmaceutical Solid-State Science: Serbia–Hungary Joint Laboratory Initiative
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: CROSSFORM supported joint research mobility and shared instrumentation access between the Faculty of Technology in Novi Sad and the Department of Pharmaceutical Technology at the University of Pécs. Radić led the work package on co-crystal characterisation methodology harmonisation, coordinating two joint experimental campaigns at Pécs (six-month stays of PhD students) and two reciprocal visits by Hungarian researchers to Novi Sad. The programme funded an upgrade to the laboratory's confocal Raman system (motorised stage, 785 nm laser line) and produced four co-authored publications and a joint summer school on pharmaceutical solid-state methods, attended by 34 students from both countries.
partners: Department of Pharmaceutical Technology, University of Pécs, Hungary
Faculty of Technology, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Sleep-Stage-Specific Interictal Epileptiform Activity as a Biomarker for Presurgical Localisation in Drug-Resistant Focal Epilepsy
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project investigates whether the distribution of interictal epileptiform discharges across sleep stages, measured by high-density EEG polysomnography, can improve non-invasive localisation of the seizure onset zone in patients being evaluated for epilepsy surgery. The study enrolls 60 drug-resistant focal epilepsy patients undergoing stereo-EEG evaluation at the Clinical Centre of Vojvodina. Polysomnographic recordings are obtained before electrode implantation and source estimates from sleep-stage-specific IED clusters are compared with iEEG-defined onset zones. Secondary aims include developing automated stage-stratified IED extraction tools in collaboration with the Faculty of Technical Sciences and examining cognitive correlates of slow-oscillation–spindle coupling disruption.
partners: Clinical Centre of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad
Department of Psychology, Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Thalamocortical Mechanisms of Sleep Disruption in Focal Epilepsy: A Multicentre Polysomnographic and Neuroimaging Study
projects.programme: bilateral
projects.summary: This bilateral Serbian–Italian project examines thalamocortical mechanisms underlying sleep macro- and microarchitecture disruption in drug-resistant focal epilepsy, combining polysomnographic data collected in Novi Sad with diffusion tensor imaging and thalamic segmentation performed in Bologna. The study compares 50 patients across three epilepsy subtypes (mesial temporal sclerosis, focal cortical dysplasia, and lesion-negative) with 50 matched healthy volunteers. Specific objectives include characterising slow-oscillation–spindle coupling asymmetries in relation to thalamic relay nucleus volume and identifying imaging–electrophysiology correlates that predict surgical outcome.
partners: Department of Neurological Sciences, University of Bologna, Italy
Faculty of Medicine, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Lexical Transfer in Habsburg Administrative Cultures: Serbian, Croatian, and Hungarian in the 18th Century
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project assembled and annotated a trilingual corpus of administrative texts in Serbian, Croatian, and Hungarian from Vojvodina and Slavonia dated 1700–1800, totalling approximately 280,000 tokens across the three languages. Its principal aim was to identify shared and divergent patterns in the borrowing of Western European commercial and legal vocabulary under Habsburg governance. The Serbian team at Novi Sad coordinated corpus preparation and lexicographic output; partners in Zagreb and Pécs contributed their respective language datasets. The project produced a shared TEI-encoded corpus deposited with CLARIN.SI, a series of comparative journal articles, and the first instalment of the annotated Serbian historical glossary. Three early-career researchers received training in historical corpus methods.
partners: Department of Croatian Language and Literature, University of Zagreb, Croatia
Department of Hungarian Linguistics, University of Pécs, Hungary
Institute for the Serbian Language, Serbian Academy of Sciences and Arts, Belgrade

projects.title: Environmental Narratives of West Africa: Literary Corpora, Teaching Materials, and Intercultural Reception in Central and Eastern Europe
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project built an annotated corpus of 40 Anglophone West African literary texts with environmental themes, developed and piloted teaching modules for use in university English literature courses in Serbia, and conducted reception research with student cohorts at the University of Novi Sad. Activities included two international workshops, a publicly accessible annotated reading list, and the curriculum study published in 2022. The project ran from the Department of English Studies with collaboration from partners in Hungary and Poland. It supported one junior researcher through a one-year contract and contributed to the MA programme in Anglophone Postcolonial Literatures at the faculty.
partners: Department of English Studies, University of Pécs
Institute of English Studies, University of Wrocław

projects.title: Autonomic Correlates of Perfectionism-Related Emotion Dysregulation in Student Populations
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: This project investigates the psychophysiological underpinnings of emotion regulation failure in non-clinical perfectionism using multimodal autonomic recording. The study protocol combines electrodermal activity, electrocardiography, and respiratory monitoring during a battery of evaluative stress tasks adapted for repeated-measures designs. A sample of approximately 150 students from the University of Novi Sad will be recruited and followed across two academic assessment periods. Primary outcomes include RSA suppression magnitude, SCL reactivity, and recovery trajectories. Filipović contributes to data collection, signal processing, and manuscript preparation. The project is coordinated by the Psychophysiology Laboratory, Department of Psychology, Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad.
partners: Department of Psychology, Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Standardizacija psihodinamskih formulacionih instrumenata u kliničko-istraživačkoj praksi zapadnog Balkana
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Projekat je imao za cilj harmonizaciju i standardizaciju instrumenata za psihodinamsku formulaciju slučaja kroz razvoj zajedničkog kodnog priručnika prilagođenog srpskom jezičkom i kulturnom kontekstu, te validaciju tog priručnika na kliničkim uzorcima iz Srbije, Bosne i Hercegovine i Crne Gore. Sprovedeno je osam višednevnih treninga za istraživače i kliniku, a finalni priručnik je javno dostupan. Projektom je obuhvaćeno 210 kliničkih slučajeva iz četiri ustanove, generisana je baza anonimizovanih intervjua i razvijena standardizovana procedura obuke procenjivača. Rezultati su objavljeni u recenziranim časopisima i prezentovani na međunarodnim konferencijama.
partners: Filozofski fakultet, Univerzitet u Novom Sadu
Klinika za psihijatriju, Klinički centar Vojvodine
Filozofski fakultet, Univerzitet u Sarajevu
Institut za mentalno zdravlje, Podgorica

projects.title: Meme Circulation and Political Discourse in Western Balkan Online Publics
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: MEMPOL investigates how political memes function as vehicles for discourse formation and fragmentation in online public spheres across Serbia, Bosnia-Herzegovina, and North Macedonia. The project combines automated corpus collection from Facebook, Telegram, and TikTok with semiotic annotation and qualitative interviews with content creators and consumers. Tihomir Pekez contributes to corpus design, the development of the multimodal annotation framework, and the analysis of Serbian-language material. The project is coordinated by the Department of Media Studies at the University of Novi Sad and includes partners from Sarajevo and Skopje. Expected outputs include an open annotated corpus, three peer-reviewed articles, and a policy brief addressed to media literacy organisations.
partners: Faculty of Political Sciences, University of Sarajevo
Institute for Communication Studies, Skopje
Department of Media Studies, Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Regulatory Transplants and Constitutional Limits: Sub-legislative Rulemaking in Western Balkan Accession States
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: Projekat ispituje ustavnopravna ograničenja prenosa normativnih ovlašćenja na regulatorna tela u Srbiji, Bosni i Hercegovini i Severnoj Makedoniji, s posebnim fokusom na tehničke oblasti pod uticajem procesa pridruživanja EU. Tim od sedam istraživača sa Pravnog fakulteta Univerziteta u Novom Sadu i partnerskih institucija analizira sistematski korpus od oko 300 podzakonskih akata i tehničkih propisa donetih između 2015. i 2023. godine. Krajnji ishodi uključuju izradu komparativne studije, bazu odluka relevantnih ustavnih i upravnih sudova u regionu, i set preporuka za zakonodavnu praksu.
partners: Faculty of Law, University of Sarajevo
Iustinianus Primus Faculty of Law, Ss. Cyril and Methodius University, Skopje
Institute for Comparative Law, Belgrade

projects.title: Digital Integration Barriers in Small and Medium Enterprises of the Serbia–Hungary Cross-Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: The project examines structural and behavioural barriers preventing SMEs in the Hungary–Serbia cross-border region from integrating digital tools into core business processes. Partner teams in Subotica and Pécs are conducting parallel firm-level surveys and a series of workshops with enterprise owners. Bojana Rajić contributes to survey instrument design, data collection in Vojvodina, and the preparation of regional comparison reports. The project will produce an openly available benchmark dataset of digitisation indicators for approximately 300 SMEs across both regions, as well as a practitioner handbook with sector-specific recommendations. Final outputs are due in late 2025 and will be disseminated through partner chambers of commerce.
partners: Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Business and Economics, University of Pécs

projects.title: Revenue Optimisation Under Asymmetric Demand Signals in Pannonian Tourism Accommodation
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project develops and validates a revenue management decision-support toolkit tailored to independently owned accommodation businesses in the Pannonian region. Core activities include assembly of a multi-year daily rate and occupancy panel from partner hotels and rental properties, estimation of asymmetric demand models that distinguish high-side and low-side forecast errors, and design of rule-based pricing triggers suitable for operators without dedicated revenue management staff. Fieldwork involves structured interviews with 80 accommodation managers and a randomised advisory intervention with 22 willing participants. Deliverables include an open-access dataset, a calibrated forecasting module, and a practitioner handbook distributed through the Tourism Organisation of Vojvodina.
partners: Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad
Tourism Organisation of Vojvodina
Institute for Economic Research, Belgrade

projects.title: Cross-Border Yield Management Benchmarking for Small Hotels in the Hungary–Serbia Border Region
projects.programme: Interreg IPA Hungary–Serbia
projects.summary: This cross-border cooperation project compared revenue management practices, technology adoption rates, and seasonal pricing outcomes in small hotels on both sides of the Hungarian–Serbian border. Krstić led the work package responsible for data collection, benchmarking methodology, and training material development on the Serbian side. The project surveyed 160 hotels (80 per country), conducted 40 paired depth interviews, and ran three joint training workshops in Subotica and Szeged attended by 140 participants. A bilingual best-practice guide was produced and distributed to regional tourism associations. The project documented a 14-percentage-point gap in revenue management tool adoption between the two sides and proposed a shared regional pricing observatory.
partners: Faculty of Economics in Subotica, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Regulatory Stakeholder Mapping Tools for SMEs in the Energy and Pharmaceutical Sectors of the Western Balkans
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: REGMAP developed a practical toolkit—combining a validated survey instrument, a facilitated workshop protocol, and a lightweight software dashboard—that allows medium-sized firms in the energy and pharmaceutical sectors to construct and update stakeholder salience maps without external consultants. The project ran in three phases: instrument validation (year 1), toolkit development and piloting with twelve partner firms in Serbia (year 2), and dissemination through NTP Novi Sad and two sectoral industry associations (year 3). The toolkit was tested against independently assessed salience maps prepared by academic researchers and achieved acceptable convergent validity. Project outputs include two journal articles, one conference contribution, and a publicly available manual. Three NTP-resident firms participated in the piloting phase.

projects.title: Transnational Approaches to Socialist-Era Film Preservation in the Adriatic–Danubian Region
projects.programme: Horizon 2020
projects.summary: A consortium project involving eight institutions from Serbia, Croatia, Slovenia, Hungary, and Austria, focused on establishing shared protocols for the preservation and digital access of socialist-era moving image materials. Babić led Work Package 3, which addressed photochemical and hybrid digitisation workflows, coordinating practice-sharing visits between laboratory facilities, conducting a comparative equipment audit across partner institutions, and co-authoring the workflow guidance document distributed to all partners. The project also produced a freely downloadable condition-assessment toolkit for small archives lacking dedicated conservation staff. Total project budget was approximately €1.9 million; the Novi Sad team managed a sub-grant of approximately €180,000 covering personnel, consumables, and equipment.

projects.title: Wearable Biosensor Systems for Participatory and Collaborative Live Performance in Southeast Europe
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: The project developed and tested an integrated wearable biosensor toolkit—combining sEMG, IMU, HRV, and EDA modalities—for deployment in collaborative live performance contexts involving multiple performers. Working with three performance groups based in Novi Sad, Belgrade, and Niš, the project produced four publicly performed works, an open-source hardware design for a custom multi-channel biosensor garment, and a software library for routing physiological data to TouchDesigner and Unity environments. The project also ran three practitioner workshops attended by 38 performance makers and digital artists from Serbia and neighbouring countries. A methodological guide for artists working with biosensors was produced in Serbian and English and distributed freely through partner institutions.
partners: Faculty of Technical Sciences, University of Novi Sad

projects.title: Mapping Net.Art Practices and Institutional Critique in Central and Eastern Europe: A Comparative Digital Archive
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: NETMAP-CEE built the first systematic digital archive and relational database of net.art and tactical media works produced in Central and Eastern Europe between 1993 and 2012. The project team, based at the Academy of Arts Novi Sad with partners in Timișoara and Prague, digitised and described 634 works in a shared metadata schema, conducted oral history interviews with forty-one practitioners, and developed a public annotation interface for researcher and community use. The project also produced two peer-reviewed articles, a doctoral dissertation supervised by Milošević, and a methodological handbook for net.art archivists distributed to twelve regional institutions. All database records are publicly accessible under a Creative Commons licence.
partners: Faculty of Arts and Design, West University of Timișoara
Academy of Arts, Architecture and Design, Prague

projects.title: Difficulty-Adaptive Instruction for Language Learning in Multilingual Classrooms of Vojvodina
projects.programme: Provincial Secretariat for Higher Education and Scientific Research
projects.summary: The project developed and tested a modular adaptive exercise engine for Serbian, Hungarian, and Slovak language learning targeted at multilingual secondary school classrooms in Vojvodina. The engine implemented a hybrid adaptation strategy combining offline IRT calibration with online Bayesian ability estimation. Classroom trials were conducted in six schools across three municipalities, involving approximately 380 students over three academic semesters. Project deliverables included a documented item bank of 1,200 calibrated grammar and vocabulary exercises, a teacher dashboard for monitoring class-level progress, and a technical report on server infrastructure requirements for school deployment. The project resulted in three peer-reviewed publications and a set of free instructional materials distributed to participating schools.
partners: Pedagogical Institute of Vojvodina, Novi Sad
Gymnasium 'Jovan Jovanović Zmaj', Novi Sad
Secondary School 'Svetozar Miletić', Subotica

projects.title: Decentralised Swarm Protocols for Mixed-Function Ground Robot Fleets in Arable and Horticultural Crops
projects.programme: Science Fund of the Republic of Serbia (PROMIS, IDEAS, Prizma)
projects.summary: FIELDSWARM investigates coordination algorithms that allow ground robot fleets composed of mechanically distinct platforms to perform complementary field operations concurrently. The project targets two use cases: inter-row weeding combined with targeted drip irrigation in maize, and under-canopy scouting combined with spot-treatment in apple orchards. Jana Brtka contributes to the design and field validation of the task-allocation and communication layers. Field trials are conducted on partner farms in Vojvodina. The project also produces open datasets of robot telemetry, soil condition measurements, and weed-density maps from the trial sites, which will be released under a Creative Commons licence at project end.
partners: BioSense Institute, University of Novi Sad
Faculty of Agriculture, University of Novi Sad
Agricultural Cooperative Ravnica, Zrenjanin
